subject: example

verseText: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.

subject: money
prompt: “For the love of money is the root of all evil” — where is this written?
verseText: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

subject: study
prompt: “Study to shew thyself approved unto God” — where is this written?
verseText: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.

subject: cretian proverb
prompt: “The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies” — from which chapter of Titus?
verseText: One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies.

verseText: And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.

subject: soldier metaphors
prompt: Which of these KJV verses is the one that says “The husbandman that laboureth must be first partaker of the fruits”?
options: The husbandman that laboureth must be first partaker of the fruits.
No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life.
And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.
For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn.
verseText: The husbandman that laboureth must be first partaker of the fruits.

subject: elders
prompt: “Holding fast the faithful word” is the exact wording of which verse?
verseText: Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.

subject: godliness
prompt: Which is the exact KJV wording of 1 Timothy 4:8?
options: For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.

subject: authority
prompt: “Let no man despise thee” (without “thy youth” coming right after it) appears in which verse?
verseText: These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.

verseText: This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;

subject: bishop qualifications
prompt: What is the exact reason a bishop must not be “a novice”?
options: lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil
lest he come into reproach and the snare of the devil
lest he be not able to rule his own house
lest he be proud, knowing nothing
verseText: Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.

options: Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.

subject: good works

options: This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works.
This is a faithful saying, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly.

subject: good fight
prompt: “Fight the good fight of faith” (1 Tim 6:12) and “I have fought a good fight” (the other pastoral epistle) — where is the second one?
verseText: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
verseTextB: Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.

subject: charge
prompt: “I charge thee therefore before God” (2 Tim 4:1) has a sister charge in 1 Timothy: “I charge thee before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels…” — which verse?
verseText: I charge thee before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality.
verseTextB: I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom;

subject: faithful sayings
prompt: “It is a faithful saying” (2 Tim 2:11) — which OTHER verse in these books also calls itself “a faithful saying”?
verseText: It is a faithful saying: For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him:
verseTextB: This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.

subject: avoid
prompt: “But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies…” (Titus 3:9). The parallel instruction in 2 Timothy says: “But ______ and unlearned questions avoid…” What's the missing word?
verseText: But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes.
verseTextB: But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.

subject: sound doctrine
prompt: “Hold fast the form of sound words” (2 Tim 1:13) pairs with “holding fast the faithful word” in Titus — for what purpose?
options: that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers
that he may be sound in the faith, sober, grave, temperate
that he may be proud, knowing nothing, doting about questions
that he may be a vessel unto honour, prepared unto every good work
verseText: Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.
verseTextB: Hold fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.

Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.

subject: charge
prompt: Synthesis: In 1 Timothy 6:20 Paul says “keep that which is committed to thy trust”; in 2 Timothy 1:14 he says “that good thing which was committed unto thee keep.” What single verb do both verses use for guarding the deposit?
verseText: That good thing which was committed unto thee keep by the Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us.

verses.verseText: O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called:
That good thing which was committed unto thee keep by the Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us.

subject: good works
prompt: Synthesis: 1 Timothy 5:10 speaks of those “diligently” following “every good work”; 2 Timothy 3:17 says the man of God is “throughly furnished unto all good works”; Titus 3:8 urges believers to “maintain good works.” What theme do all three tie to?
verseText: This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.

verses.verseText: Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.
That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.

This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.

verseText: A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject;

And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus; Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some.
